en.summary: Claim 1 describes a method of selectively programming an individual memory cell of a non-volatile memory array. Each cell includes a well of a first conductivity type, a diffusion drain of that type encompassed by a localized well region of a second conductivity type in the well, a diffusion source of the first type formed laterally adjacent to that localized well region, an isolated charge trapping layer between the drain and source over the localized well region and the well, and a gate above that layer. The method comprises applying a first voltage, simultaneously, to the diffusion drain and the localized well region of a selected said memory cell through a selected bit line; floating the diffusion source of the selected memory cell; and applying a second voltage to the gate of the selected memory cell, thereby inducing Fowler-Nordheim (FN) tunneling at least between the isolated charge trapping layer and the localized well region. This is a technical reading of the printed claim, not a legal construction.
limitations: A method of selectively programming an individual memory cell of a non-volatile memory array.

Providing an array of memory cells, each including a well of a first conductivity type, a diffusion drain of that type encompassed by a localized well region of a second conductivity type in the well, a diffusion source of the first type laterally formed adjacent to that localized well region in the well, an isolated charge trapping layer located between the drain and source over the localized well region and the well, and a gate above the isolated charge trapping layer.
Applying a first voltage, simultaneously, to the diffusion drain and the localized well region of a selected said memory cell through a selected bit line.
Floating the diffusion source of the selected memory cell.
Applying a second voltage to the gate of the selected memory cell, thereby inducing Fowler-Nordheim (FN) tunneling at least between the isolated charge trapping layer and the localized well region.
en.dependentClaimBoundary: Claims 2–3 further recite conductivity types and voltages of about 3~7 volts and about −7~−3 volts. Claims 4–5 further concern whether the diffusion source partially overlaps the localized well region. Claim 6 further requires the charge trapping layer to be composed of silicon nitride. Claims 7, 14 and 18 are additional independent method claims involving hot-hole injection or other bias combinations. Claims end at Claim 20. These are not limitations of Claim 1 alone.
en.specificationBoundary: FIGS. 1, 2 and 2A are prior art. FIG. 3 and the specification describe a first-embodiment ONO cell and program/erase voltage tables. Example voltages, hot-electron or hot-hole mechanisms and performance comparisons in the specification are not added numerical limitations of Claim 1 and are not measured-performance evidence in this review.
en.unknowns: Actual FN tunneling, selectivity, operating voltages and any measured results were not established. The front page recites a 0-day 35 U.S.C. 154(b) adjustment. Complete global family, current ownership, legal status and product mapping remain unverified.

en.summary: Claim 1 describes a structure of an embedded channel write/erase flash memory cell, comprising mainly an N-substrate, a flash memory cell region and a CMOS device region. The flash memory cell region comprises mainly a deep P-well in the substrate; N-well formed in that deep P-well, with a deep p-type region and a shallow p-type region implanted in predetermined positions of the N-well; a first n-type region formed at one side of the shallow p-type region and in the deep p-type region to be used as a drain; a second n-type region formed at the other side of the shallow p-type region to be used as a source; and a stacked gate formed on the N-well. The CMOS device region comprises mainly a first deep P-well and a first N-well therein with a plurality of p-type regions implanted in predetermined positions, and a second deep P-well and a second N-well therein with a plurality of p-type regions implanted in predetermined positions. This is a technical reading of the printed claim, not a legal construction.
limitations: A structure of an embedded channel write/erase flash memory cell, comprising mainly an N-substrate, a flash memory cell region and a CMOS device region.

The flash memory cell region comprises mainly a deep P-well formed in the substrate, and N-well formed in that deep P-well, with a deep p-type region and a shallow p-type region implanted in predetermined positions of the N-well.

A first n-type region formed at one side of the shallow p-type region and in the deep p-type region in the N-well to be used as a drain, and a second n-type region formed at the other side of the shallow p-type region in the N-well to be used as a source.
A stacked gate formed on the N-well.

The CMOS device region comprises mainly a first deep P-well in the substrate and a first N-well therein with a plurality of p-type regions implanted in predetermined positions, and a second deep P-well in the substrate and a second N-well therein with a plurality of p-type regions implanted in predetermined positions.

en.summary: Claim 1 describes a method for programming a PMOS single-transistor memory unit. The unit comprises a silicon dioxide-silicon nitride-silicon dioxide (ONO) dielectric stack on an N-well, a P type polysilicon gate on that stack, a P type doped source region in the N-well at one side of the gate, and a P type doped drain region in the N-well on the other side of the gate. The method comprises biasing the gate to a word line voltage VWL; biasing the source region to a source line voltage VSL greater than VWL, wherein |VWL-VSL| is larger than threshold voltage of the unit, so as to provide an adequate gate-to-source bias to turn on a P-channel; biasing the drain region to a bit line voltage VBL smaller than VSL, so as to provide a lateral electric field that forces P-channel hot holes through the P-channel in an accelerated drift rate to the drain region, thereby inducing hot electrons near the drain region, some of induced hot electrons being injected into the ONO stack; and biasing the N-well to a well voltage VNW equal to VSL. This is a technical reading of the printed claim, not a legal construction.
limitations: A method for programming a PMOS single-transistor memory unit comprising an ONO dielectric stack on an N-well, a P type polysilicon gate on that stack, and P type doped source and drain regions in the N-well on opposite sides of the gate.
Biasing the P type polysilicon gate to a word line voltage VWL.

Biasing the P type doped source region to a source line voltage VSL greater than VWL, wherein |VWL-VSL| is larger than threshold voltage of the unit, so as to provide an adequate gate-to-source bias to turn on a P-channel.

Biasing the P type doped drain region to a bit line voltage VBL smaller than VSL, so as to provide a lateral electric field that forces P-channel hot holes through the P-channel in an accelerated drift rate to the drain region, thereby inducing hot electrons near the drain region, and wherein some of induced hot electrons are injected into the ONO dielectric stack.
Biasing the N-well to a well voltage VNW equal to the source line voltage VSL.

claim1Verbatim: A fabrication method for a metal oxide semiconductor transistor of a non-volatile memory, the method comprising: forming a first doped region, a second doped region and a third doped region on a well; forming a control gate between the first doped region and the second doped region; forming a floating gate between the second doped region and the third doped region; providing a first biasing voltage between the first doped region and the control gate such that the first doped region and the second doped region are conductive; providing a second biasing voltage between the second doped region and the well, so as to generate a channel current between the second doped region and the third doped region, and generate a gate current; wherein if a voltage difference between the third doped region and the floating gate is smaller than a value of a threshold voltage of the metal-oxide-semiconductor transistor, increasing a capacitance between the floating gate and the third doped region to larger than a total capacitance synthesized between the floating gate and the well, the floating gate and the second doped region, and the floating gate and the control gate; or increasing a capacitance between the floating gate and the control gate to larger than a total capacitance synthesized between the floating gate and the third doped region, the floating gate and the well, and the floating gate and the second doped region; wherein if a voltage difference between the third doped region and the floating gate is larger than the threshold voltage, decreasing the capacitance between the floating gate and the third doped region to smaller than the total capacitance synthesized between the floating gate and the well, the floating gate and the second doped region, and the floating gate and the control gate; and decreasing the capacitance between the floating gate and the control gate to smaller than the total capacitance synthesized between the floating gate and the third doped region, the floating gate and the well, and the floating gate and the second doped region.

zh.summary: Claim 1 描述一種非揮發性記憶體金屬氧化物半導體電晶體的製造方法，包含：在井上形成第一、第二與第三摻雜區；在第一與第二摻雜區之間形成控制閘；在第二與第三摻雜區之間形成浮閘；在第一摻雜區與控制閘之間提供第一偏壓，使第一與第二摻雜區導通；在第二摻雜區與井之間提供第二偏壓，以在第二與第三摻雜區之間產生通道電流並產生閘極電流；以及依第三摻雜區與浮閘之間的電壓差相對於該金屬氧化物半導體電晶體臨界電壓的大小，增大或減小浮閘與第三摻雜區之間、以及浮閘與控制閘之間的電容，使其分別大於或小於浮閘與其餘節點所合成的總電容。請求項前言寫作 “metal oxide semiconductor”，其後條件則寫作 “metal-oxide-semiconductor transistor”，依印刷原文保留。以下為公報請求項原文的技術導讀，不是法律上的權利範圍判定。
limitations: 一種非揮發性記憶體金屬氧化物半導體電晶體的製造方法，包含在井上形成第一、第二與第三摻雜區。
在第一與第二摻雜區之間形成控制閘。
在第二與第三摻雜區之間形成浮閘。
在第一摻雜區與控制閘之間提供第一偏壓，使第一與第二摻雜區導通。
在第二摻雜區與井之間提供第二偏壓，以在第二與第三摻雜區之間產生通道電流，並產生閘極電流。
若第三摻雜區與浮閘之間的電壓差小於該金屬氧化物半導體電晶體臨界電壓的一個值，則將浮閘與第三摻雜區之間的電容增大至大於浮閘與井、浮閘與第二摻雜區及浮閘與控制閘所合成的總電容；或將浮閘與控制閘之間的電容增大至大於浮閘與第三摻雜區、浮閘與井及浮閘與第二摻雜區所合成的總電容。
若第三摻雜區與浮閘之間的電壓差大於該臨界電壓，則將浮閘與第三摻雜區之間的電容減小至小於上述合成總電容，並將浮閘與控制閘之間的電容減小至小於浮閘與第三摻雜區、浮閘與井及浮閘與第二摻雜區所合成的總電容。

en.summary: Claim 1 describes a fabrication method for a metal oxide semiconductor transistor of a non-volatile memory, comprising forming first, second and third doped regions on a well; forming a control gate between the first and second doped regions; forming a floating gate between the second and third doped regions; providing a first biasing voltage between the first doped region and the control gate such that the first and second doped regions are conductive; providing a second biasing voltage between the second doped region and the well so as to generate a channel current between the second and third doped regions and generate a gate current; and, depending on whether a voltage difference between the third doped region and the floating gate is smaller or larger than a threshold voltage of the metal-oxide-semiconductor transistor, increasing or decreasing capacitances between the floating gate and the third doped region and between the floating gate and the control gate relative to a synthesized total capacitance with the remaining nodes. The preamble prints “metal oxide semiconductor,” while a later clause prints “metal-oxide-semiconductor transistor”; both are transcribed as printed. This is a technical reading of the printed claim, not a legal construction.
limitations: A fabrication method for a metal oxide semiconductor transistor of a non-volatile memory, comprising forming a first doped region, a second doped region and a third doped region on a well.
Forming a control gate between the first doped region and the second doped region.
Forming a floating gate between the second doped region and the third doped region.
Providing a first biasing voltage between the first doped region and the control gate such that the first doped region and the second doped region are conductive.

Providing a second biasing voltage between the second doped region and the well, so as to generate a channel current between the second doped region and the third doped region, and generate a gate current.

If a voltage difference between the third doped region and the floating gate is smaller than a value of a threshold voltage of the metal-oxide-semiconductor transistor, increasing a capacitance between the floating gate and the third doped region to larger than a total capacitance synthesized between the floating gate and the well, the floating gate and the second doped region, and the floating gate and the control gate; or increasing a capacitance between the floating gate and the control gate to larger than a total capacitance synthesized between the floating gate and the third doped region, the floating gate and the well, and the floating gate and the second doped region.

If a voltage difference between the third doped region and the floating gate is larger than the threshold voltage, decreasing the capacitance between the floating gate and the third doped region to smaller than the total capacitance synthesized between the floating gate and the well, the floating gate and the second doped region, and the floating gate and the control gate; and decreasing the capacitance between the floating gate and the control gate to smaller than the total capacitance synthesized between the floating gate and the third doped region, the floating gate and the well, and the floating gate and the second doped region.

These are not limitations of Claim 1 alone.

en.summary: Claim 1 describes a read-only memory (ROM) cell unit comprising a P type substrate, an N well in that substrate, a non-stacked gate electrode PMOS select transistor formed on the N well, and a non-stacked gate electrode PMOS floating gate transistor printed as formed on the “N wall” and serially electrically connected to the select transistor. The select transistor comprises a select gate electrically connected to a word line, a first P+ source doping region electrically connected to a source line, and a first P+ drain doping region. The floating-gate transistor comprises a floating gate, a second P+ source doping region electrically connected to the first P+ drain doping region, and a second P+ drain doping region electrically connected to a bit line. The printed claim then states that “the second P+ source doping region and the second P+ source doping region define a floating gate channel.” P type impurities are implanted into the floating gate P channel, thereby turning the floating-gate transistor into a depletion-mode transistor for storing logic data “1.” Missing articles in the printed wording are retained. This is a technical reading of the printed claim, not a legal construction.
limitations: A ROM cell unit comprising a P type substrate and an N well disposed in the P type substrate.

A non-stacked gate electrode PMOS select transistor formed on the N well, comprising a select gate electrically connected to a word line, a first P+ source doping region electrically connected to a source line, and a first P+ drain doping region.

A non-stacked gate electrode PMOS floating gate transistor printed as formed on the “N wall” and serially electrically connected to the select transistor, comprising a floating gate, a second P+ source doping region electrically connected to the first P+ drain doping region, and a second P+ drain doping region electrically connected to a bit line.
The printed claim states that the second P+ source doping region and the second P+ source doping region define a floating gate channel.
P type impurities are implanted into the floating gate P channel, thereby turning the floating-gate transistor into a depletion-mode transistor for storing logic data “1.”

en.summary: Claim 1 describes a control method of a non-volatile memory. en.summary: Claim 1 describes a method for operating a register stage having a first latch and a second latch arranged in a master-slave flip-flop configuration for storing a first bit of data and a second bit of data respectively, comprising: a) decoupling the first latch from a serial input terminal and decoupling the second latch from the first latch at the same time while a source clock signal oscillates; and, b) initiating a shifting operation on either a high logic level of the source clock or a low logic level of the source clock for shifting one of the first bit of data and the second bit of data. The printed wording “and,” after “oscillates” is retained. This is a technical reading of the printed claim, not a legal construction.
limitations: A method for operating a register stage having a first latch and a second latch arranged in a master-slave flip-flop configuration for storing a first bit of data and a second bit of data respectively.
Decoupling the first latch from a serial input terminal and decoupling the second latch from the first latch at the same time while a source clock signal oscillates.
Initiating a shifting operation on either a high logic level of the source clock or a low logic level of the source clock for shifting one of the first bit of data and the second bit of data.
en.dependentClaimBoundary: Claim 2 further recites that the step of decoupling includes turning off a first gating device between the first latch and a serial input terminal and turning off a second gating device between the first latch and the second latch. Claim 5 further recites that the step of initiating includes turning on the first gating device while the second gating device is turned off for shifting the second bit of data. Claims 2–10 depend from Claim 1 or earlier dependents; no other independent claim was observed. Claims end at Claim 10. These are not limitations of Claim 1 alone.
en.specificationBoundary: FIGS. 1–3 are all labeled prior art, and together with the background they describe the basic circuit, planar and cross-sectional views of an anti-fuse memory cell. Those details are disclosure, not added Claim 1 limitations, and are not measured-performance evidence in this review.
